text: Git branching is an important part of any version control workflow. A branch lets you work on new ideas without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build a single feature or fix a bug safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes and discuss them. This simple workflow keeps the project organized and reduces mistakes. It also allows several people to work at the same time without causing conflicts, making teamwork smoother and more efficient.
